hub.title: Climbing Board Apps | Boardsesh
hub.description: Find a climbing board app for Kilter, Tension, MoonBoard, Woods and more. Check compatible layouts, LED control and logbook imports before installing.
hub.heading: One climbing app for your boards
hub.intro: Boardsesh keeps sends from different boards in one logbook. In a solo 4x4, it counts logged reps and moves to the next climb after the set rest. Whether it’s worth switching depends on how you climb and which controller is on your wall. Choose your board for a comparison with its official app.
hub.compatibility: Each guide covers the supported layouts, LED controllers and logbook imports for that board. For a wall with your own hold placement, start with the spray wall comparison.
hub.tradeoffs: You can try Boardsesh in a browser before installing. Browser LED control needs Web Bluetooth and a compatible controller. On iPhone, use the native app to light the holds.

platformDesign.title: Designed for iPhone and Android
platformDesign.body: Apple’s Human Interface Guidelines shape the default iOS experience, from system tabs to text that follows your Dynamic Type setting. Liquid Glass is available on iOS 26, with a blur fallback on earlier supported versions. Android’s default Material Design 3 layout uses bottom tabs on phones and moves navigation to a side rail when a tablet window has room.

kilter.title: Kilter Board App Guide | Boardsesh
kilter.description: Use Boardsesh on Kilter Board Original or Homewall. Preview climbs from hold thumbnails, share a queue, and import your Kilter or Aurora logbook.
kilter.heading: Boardsesh for Kilter Board
kilter.intro: Boardsesh puts the holds right in the climb list. On a Kilter Board Original or Homewall, you can scan those thumbnails, swipe through previews and light a problem from your iPhone or Android phone.
kilter.compatibility: Boardsesh supports Kilter Board Original and Homewall. Match the wall size, installed hold sets and angle to get the right climb list. Lighting the holds requires a compatible Bluetooth controller.
kilter.tradeoffs: If your crew wants to add problems from their own phones, use Boardsesh. It also starts importing an old Aurora logbook as soon as you confirm the file. Keep Kilter’s app for managing your Kilter profile, reclaiming setter credit or logging new activity in that account.
kilter.screenshotAlt: Boardsesh displaying a Kilter climb with the starting, middle and finishing holds marked

layout.title: Original and Homewall
layout.body: The layout at your gym or home determines which problems you’ll see. Start with Original or Homewall, then set the size, hold sets and angle. Once the app has the right wall, you can browse by grade or filter for Kilter’s Verified climbs.

preview.title: Climb controls within thumb reach
preview.body: In the default phone layout, Put on board, the queue and logging sit below the board image. Open the queue or log in a sheet over the climb. By default, the sheets use the system appearance on iPhone and Material 3 on Android. The log sheet keeps Attempt and the save controls within thumb reach at the bottom. When you’re scrolled to the top of the climb view, a swipe down closes it.

training.title: A new problem on each interval
training.body: An On the Minute block is useful when you want the next Kilter problem ready on a schedule. Set the target grade and interval, then review the climbs before creating the session. Tap Start workout when you’re ready for the first countdown. In a solo session, the timer brings up the next queued problem as each interval ends.

import.title: Your current Kilter account
import.body: Link your current account in Settings → Connected apps to copy sends, attempts, ratings and circuits. Boardsesh encrypts the token it stores. If you use social-only sign-in or two-factor authentication, tap Import on the Kilter (new) card instead. New ticks you log in Boardsesh stay here.

auroraImport.title: The file from the old Kilter app
auroraImport.body: History from the old Kilter app comes from Aurora. If you haven’t received your JSON export, request it from Aurora first. With the file in hand, tap Import on the Kilter (Aurora) card in Settings → Connected apps and confirm the preview. The import starts right away and shows progress on your phone.

discovery.label: Find climbs
discovery.boardsesh: See the holds in the list thumbnails and swipe between climb previews. Filter by grade or for Kilter’s Verified climbs.
discovery.official: Browse by grade and other filters, including Verified climbs selected by Kilter.

climbControls.label: Climb view and controls
climbControls.boardsesh: The default phone layout puts lighting, logging and queue controls below the board image. Queue and log sheets follow iOS conventions or Android Material 3.
climbControls.official: Kilter’s published screenshot shows Back at the top left and logging controls at the bottom.

session.label: Climb with others
session.boardsesh: Light the holds over Bluetooth and build a live queue together from separate phones.
session.official: Connect to the LEDs over Bluetooth, view the board map and share climbs.

training.label: Build and run a workout
training.boardsesh: Build blocks at your chosen grades. After Start workout, timed blocks set the pace. In a solo On the Minute block, the running timer advances the queue at each interval.
training.official: Kilter documents playlists for organizing climbs and putting together training circuits.

history.label: Current Kilter account
history.boardsesh: Copy your current Kilter history into a logbook across board brands. New ticks stay in Boardsesh.
history.official: Log attempts and sends directly in your Kilter account.

auroraImportTiming.label: Old Aurora import timing
auroraImportTiming.boardsesh: With the Aurora JSON in hand, confirm the preview to import it directly into Boardsesh. The import starts right away and shows progress in the app.
auroraImportTiming.official: Kilter’s Claim Data page estimates 5–7 business days after upload. Some climbers in an April 2026 Reddit thread reported waiting weeks.

tension.title: Tension Board App Guide for TB1 and TB2 | Boardsesh
tension.description: Climb on Tension Board 1 or TB2 Mirror and Spray with Boardsesh. Find problems, run a workout and import your Tension logbook.
tension.heading: Boardsesh for Tension Board
tension.intro: Boardsesh brings TB1, TB2 Mirror and TB2 Spray into the same app on iPhone and Android. Find climbs at your wall angle, light the holds and log sends alongside your climbs on other boards.
tension.compatibility: Boardsesh supports Tension Board 1 and both Tension Board 2 layouts. TB2 Spray uses Tension’s factory hold layout. For a wall where you placed the holds yourself, use the photo-based spray wall setup.
tension.tradeoffs: Use Boardsesh for a solo 4x4 if you want the timer and queue to follow the reps you log. It’s also a fit for crews who want to add problems from separate phones. Tension’s Workout AI can build a climb list from your logbook and workout type.
tension.screenshotAlt: Boardsesh displaying a Tension Board climb and its marked holds

layout.title: Mirror and Spray are different layouts
layout.body: The board profile should match the holds in front of you, along with the wall’s dimensions and angle. On a TB2, the difference between Mirror and Spray matters as soon as you light a climb. If the LEDs show a different problem from the diagram, check the selected layout first.

training.title: The app counts your reps
training.body: A default Boardsesh 4x4 is four climbs, each done four times in a row. Set your target grade and the rests between reps and sets. Once the session is set up, tap Start workout and log each go as an attempt or send. The rep count tells you where you are in the set, and the countdown tells you when to pull on again.

import.title: Your Tension history comes with you
import.body: Link your Tension account in Settings → Connected apps to copy its logbook into Boardsesh. If your history is in an Aurora JSON export, you can upload that file there too. The import is one way. New ticks you log in Boardsesh stay here.

layout.label: Walls
layout.boardsesh: TB1 and both TB2 layouts, Mirror and Spray, alongside other board brands in the same app.
layout.official: Aurora lists the Tension app for TB1 and TB2. Tension documents both Mirror and Spray for TB2.

training.label: Build and run a workout
training.boardsesh: In a solo 4x4, each logged go counts toward the set. The app keeps the current climb up during rep rests and advances the queue when the set rest ends.
training.official: Workout AI builds a personalized climb list from your workout type and logbook. Tension also offers circuits and a timer.

history.label: Log sends
history.boardsesh: Copy your Tension history in and keep a single logbook across the boards you climb.
history.official: Log ascents and see your history in the Tension app.

moonboard.title: MoonBoard App Guide | Boardsesh
moonboard.description: Browse MoonBoard Benchmarks and Mini MoonBoard climbs in Boardsesh. Check your hold setup, supported legacy LED controllers and CSV import.
moonboard.heading: Boardsesh for MoonBoard
moonboard.intro: Getting on a MoonBoard starts with the holds on your wall. Boardsesh for iPhone and Android lets you find Benchmarks for that setup, follow the numbered grid and share a warm-up queue.
moonboard.compatibility: Boardsesh covers the 2010, 2016, Masters 2017, Masters 2019 and 2024 setups, plus Mini MoonBoard 2020 and 2025. The LED compatibility list is shorter. A Boardsesh code audit found support for the legacy Nordic UART and RedBear profiles. The third legacy profile and the Pro controller are unsupported.
moonboard.tradeoffs: Boardsesh keeps your MoonBoard logbook together with your climbs on other boards. Our compatibility findings for the legacy Nordic UART and RedBear profiles come from a code audit. Try one climb on your hardware to confirm the LEDs work. Use Moon’s app for the Pro controller or to publish problems to MoonBoard.
moonboard.screenshotAlt: Boardsesh displaying a MoonBoard climb on its numbered hold grid

setup.title: Benchmarks for the holds you have
setup.body: The year in the app names the hold setup. Match it to the holds installed on your board, then set the wall angle to find Benchmarks you can climb there. Mini MoonBoard has its own grid and climb lists, so look under the Mini setup for your wall.

controller.title: Climbing with or without LEDs
controller.body: The supported legacy controller profiles come from a code audit. If yours matches, connect and try lighting one problem before the session. The on-screen grid and logbook still work with the LEDs off.

training.title: Rest, then try the same problem again
training.body: Build a Limit Bouldering block at the grade you want to work, set a rest and review the problems for your wall. After you tap Start workout in a solo session, logging a fall starts the rest and keeps the problem up for your next try. Log a flash or send and the next problem comes up after that rest.

import.title: What comes over from a MoonBoard CSV
import.body: The MoonBoard card in Settings → Connected apps takes a CSV export. Boardsesh copies the logbook entries it can match to climbs, so those attempts and sends can sit alongside your other board sessions. New ticks you log in Boardsesh stay here.

benchmarks.label: Find problems
benchmarks.boardsesh: Browse by setup and angle and filter for Benchmarks.
benchmarks.official: Browse by hold setup, including Benchmarks curated by MoonBoard moderators.

lighting.label: LED control
lighting.boardsesh: The code supports legacy Nordic UART and RedBear profiles. Check your controller before relying on the LEDs.
lighting.official: Moon supports its LED system in the official app and publishes hardware and setup instructions.

training.label: Build and run a workout
training.boardsesh: With a rest set for solo Limit Bouldering, logging a fall starts the countdown and keeps the same climb up. Log a flash or send to advance after the rest.
training.official: Save problem lists for warm-ups, projects and training circuits in the MoonBoard app.

history.label: Log a session
history.boardsesh: Copy matching entries from a CSV into one logbook across supported boards. Future ticks stay in Boardsesh.
history.official: Log sessions and save problem lists to your MoonBoard account.

decoy.title: Decoy Board App Guide | Boardsesh
decoy.description: Use Boardsesh on the Decoy Dungeon Trainer. Choose your wall size, light climbs, share turns with your crew and bring over your Aurora logbook.
decoy.heading: Boardsesh for Decoy Board
decoy.intro: The widest Dungeon Trainer gives setters room to work out near the sides. If you climb on an eight-foot Decoy, check that the problem actually fits your wall before you line up a session.
decoy.compatibility: In Boardsesh, choose Dungeon Trainer and match your wall to the 8 × 10, 8 × 12 or 12 × 12 layout before pairing with a compatible Decoy LED kit.
decoy.tradeoffs: Keep the official Decoy Board app for Selects and leaderboards, or when you want to find problems that run along the edges. Boardsesh makes sense if your crew wants to add problems to one queue from their own phones, or if you want to keep Decoy sends in the same logbook as your other boards.
decoy.screenshotAlt: Decoy Board Dungeon Trainer layout with rows of coloured holds and dense footholds

size.title: The edges are part of the climb
size.body: Set the wall size first to see problems you can climb on the holds in front of you. Then set the angle and search by grade. On a 12 × 12, the official Decoy app’s side-climb filter is handy if you want to look along the edges.

turns.title: Pick something while your friend climbs
turns.body: Once a phone is connected to the LEDs, a shared session gives everyone access to the same queue. The next climber can add their pick during a burn, and the connected phone can light it when the wall is free.

training.title: A volume day on Decoy
training.body: For a volume day, pick a target grade and let a Volume block suggest problems. The preview shows what’s available at the angle you’ll actually climb.

history.title: The sends you already logged
history.body: The Decoy card in Settings → Connected apps can link your Aurora account or take an Aurora JSON export. Either option copies existing history into Boardsesh. Ticks you log after the move stay in Boardsesh.

search.label: Choose a problem
search.boardsesh: Browse the Dungeon Trainer by wall size and angle, then narrow the list by grade.
search.official: Find Selects or use the side-climb filter to look for problems near the left or right edge.

session.label: Climb and log
session.boardsesh: Light problems on a compatible Decoy kit from a shared queue and log sends alongside your other boards.
session.official: Light a problem with the Decoy LED kit, look for beta videos and log ascents or attempts in the app.

touchstone.title: Touchstone Board App Guide | Boardsesh
touchstone.description: Climb on the Touchstone Winter 2020 board with Boardsesh. Find problems, light compatible LEDs and bring over your Aurora history.
touchstone.heading: Boardsesh for Touchstone Board
touchstone.intro: A Winter 2020 project can stay on your list after you leave the gym. Save it in Boardsesh and next time you’re at the Touchstone Board, you can pull up the problem and see your last attempts.
touchstone.compatibility: The Boardsesh layout is Touchstone → Winter 2020 → Full Size. For gym membership, check-ins or classes, use Touchstone Climbing’s gym services.
touchstone.tradeoffs: Use Boardsesh if you split your time between the Winter 2020 wall and other training boards and want to keep your attempts together. The official Touchstone Board app is where to go for its beta videos and climber profiles.
touchstone.screenshotAlt: Touchstone Board Winter 2020 layout with blue and pink holds

wall.title: The layout at your gym
wall.body: The Full Size hold map is for the Winter 2020 board. Once you’ve matched that layout and set the angle, you can follow the diagram on your phone or light the holds with a compatible kit.

project.title: A shortlist worth keeping
project.body: If a problem needs another day, save it to a playlist with the other climbs you want to revisit. Log the attempts you put in today so you can pull up the problem and see your history next time.

training.title: What’s available at your grade
training.body: Grade Focus can build a workout around a target grade on the Winter 2020 layout. The preview shows what it found at your angle. That’s the place to check how many problems you’ll have before the session.

history.title: An existing Touchstone logbook
history.body: If your attempts and sends are already in an Aurora account, you can bring them with you using the Touchstone card in Connected apps. It accepts an account link or an Aurora JSON export. New entries stay in Boardsesh.

session.label: Find and light problems
session.boardsesh: Search the Winter 2020 catalogue, choose a problem to light or add it to a shared queue.
session.official: Search for Touchstone problems, watch available beta, create climbs and connect to the board’s LED kit.

history.label: Revisit a project
history.boardsesh: Open your Touchstone attempts and sends in the same logbook you use for other supported boards.
history.official: Log attempts or ascents and look up your history on individual problems in the Touchstone app.

grasshopper.title: Grasshopper Board App Guide | Boardsesh
grasshopper.description: Use Boardsesh on Grasshopper 2020 Ninja, Master and GrandMaster walls. Match your size, light problems and import your Aurora logbook.
grasshopper.heading: Boardsesh for Grasshopper Board
grasshopper.intro: On an adjustable Grasshopper, you might work the same problem at two angles in one session. In Boardsesh, each attempt goes in your logbook with the angle you climbed.
grasshopper.compatibility: Match Grasshopper 2020 to Ninja (8 × 10), Master (8 × 12) or GrandMaster (12 × 12). Pick the installed hold set, including the Tweener option where it applies, before connecting to a compatible kit.
grasshopper.tradeoffs: Use Boardsesh if you want to keep track of attempts at different angles alongside your sessions on other boards, or if a group wants one queue. Use the official Grasshopper Board app if you want to set in its catalogue and look up or share beta there.
grasshopper.screenshotAlt: Grasshopper 2020 GrandMaster layout with dark holds and blue accents

kit.title: The hold set matters as much as the size
kit.body: Ninja, Master and GrandMaster span different areas of the wall. The dimensions tell you which layout to open. Check the installed holds too, since the available climbs depend on the hold set you choose.

angle.title: One problem at two angles
angle.body: If you come back to a problem after changing the angle, set the new angle in the app before you log it. Boardsesh records the angle with the attempt or send, so you can see how steep the wall was for each entry.

training.title: Working up to a harder grade
training.body: A pyramid starts below your target grade, works up to it and comes back down. Boardsesh can suggest the problems for that workout. Check the preview for the holds and angle you’ll be climbing.

history.title: Sends from the Grasshopper app
history.body: If you’ve been keeping track in the official app, Grasshopper’s Connected apps card can copy the logbook from your Aurora account or take its JSON export. Your new Boardsesh ticks stay here.

search.label: Find a wall and problem
search.boardsesh: Start from the Grasshopper 2020 layout and installed holds, then search for problems at your training angle.
search.official: Find problems in the Grasshopper catalogue, create new ones and look up or share beta videos.

session.label: Light climbs and track sends
session.boardsesh: Light problems on a compatible kit, share the queue with friends and log alongside your other boards.
session.official: Connect to the Grasshopper LED kit to light the chosen problem and log ascents in the app.

so-ill.title: So iLL Connect Board App Guide | Boardsesh
so-ill.description: Use Boardsesh on 8 × 12 and 12 × 12 So iLL Connect Boards. Find Summer 2024 climbs, light the wall and share a queue.
so-ill.heading: Boardsesh for So iLL Connect Board
so-ill.intro: When friends show up at the So iLL Connect Board with different projects in mind, they can put them in the same Boardsesh queue. Each climber adds their pick from their own phone.
so-ill.compatibility: Choose So iLL Summer 2024, then match the 8 × 12 or 12 × 12 wall. The wider board has more hold columns. Use the matching layout before sending a problem to a compatible Connect Board LED kit.
so-ill.tradeoffs: Try Boardsesh if you want people to add their own problems to the queue and keep their ticks alongside other board sends. The official So iLL Board app is the choice if you want to follow climbers and share beta in its community.
so-ill.screenshotAlt: So iLL Connect Board Summer 2024 layout with rows of round holds

layout.title: Check the width before you pick a problem
layout.body: Both widths use the Summer 2024 layout. If you’re visiting a gym and aren’t sure which one you’re looking at, check the wall dimensions before choosing. The 12 × 12 has more hold columns available to setters.

crew.title: Everyone gets to add a pick
crew.body: The crew can share a queue even though one phone is connected to the LED kit. If a friend has a project in mind while someone else is climbing, they can pull it up and add it from their own phone.

training.title: When the list runs short
training.body: A Volume block can pull together problems at a target grade for your size and angle. Check the workout preview before you start. If it finds fewer problems than you planned, you can adjust the block.

history.title: The logbook you bring with you
history.body: Open Settings → Connected apps for the So iLL import. Link the Aurora account or use its JSON export to copy your history into Boardsesh. Ticks you add in Boardsesh stay there.

search.label: Browse and set
search.boardsesh: Choose the 8 × 12 or 12 × 12 Connect Board and browse problems for the Summer 2024 layout.
search.official: Search and create So iLL problems, then share beta videos or follow other climbers in the app.

session.label: Light and log
session.boardsesh: Light a climb from the crew’s queue with compatible hardware, then log your attempts and sends across boards.
session.official: Connect to the So iLL LED kit and record ascents in the official app’s logbook.

woods.title: Woods Board App Guide | Boardsesh
woods.description: Browse Woods Board climbs in Boardsesh with matching and feet rules. Check your 8 × 10 or 12 × 12 layout before lighting a problem.
woods.heading: Boardsesh for Woods Board
woods.intro: Two Woods Board problems can share the same handholds and climb differently if one rules out matching or limits the feet. Boardsesh puts both rules in the climb details.
woods.compatibility: Boardsesh supports the 8 × 10 and 12 × 12 Woods Board. Each size has its own hold and LED map. Use a compatible Woods controller to light the problem, or read the hold diagram on your phone.
woods.tradeoffs: Use the Woods Board app to keep using your existing Woods account, climb for its leaderboards or publish to its official database. Boardsesh has no Woods account import. It’s a fit if you want to log new Woods sends in the same place as the other boards you climb.
woods.screenshotAlt: Woods Board Original 12 × 12 layout with wooden handholds and footholds

size.title: Two sizes, two hold maps
size.body: Pick the layout installed on your wall before selecting a problem. The name and shape of the board can look familiar across sizes, but the map drives both the on-screen diagram and which holds light up on a compatible controller.

rules.title: Matching and feet are separate rules
rules.body: Read both in the climb details before you pull on. A problem can allow you to match a handhold and still limit you to designated feet. When you create a problem, you can set those two rules yourself.

session.title: Where your new problems and ticks go
session.body: If you set and publish a problem in Boardsesh, it goes into the Boardsesh catalogue. Your attempts and sends go into your Boardsesh logbook. For publishing to the official database, set the problem in the Woods Board app.

training.title: A workout built from the climbs you have
training.body: Grade Focus draws from problems for your Woods size and angle. If the preview comes back short, trim the block or open up the filters. The preview gives you a chance to change the plan before you get on the wall.

rules.label: Set matching and feet rules
rules.boardsesh: View or set separate matching and feet rules for problems on the hold map for your wall size.
rules.official: When a setter publishes a problem, the official app lets them specify the rules for climbing it.

history.label: Track sends
history.boardsesh: Start logging Woods sends alongside sends on your other boards. Woods accounts and history can’t be imported.
history.official: Keep logging on your existing Woods account and take part in the official Woods leaderboards.

publishing.label: Publish new problems
publishing.boardsesh: Problems you publish in Boardsesh go into the Boardsesh catalogue for the Woods layout you chose.
publishing.official: Submit new problems to the official Woods Board database, where other users of the Woods app can find them.

spray-wall-apps.title: Spray Wall Apps Compared: Stōkt and Retro Flash | Boardsesh
spray-wall-apps.description: Compare Boardsesh, Stōkt and Retro Flash for a home or gym spray wall. See photo setup, sharing, circuits, optional LED control and pricing.
spray-wall-apps.heading: Compare spray wall climbing apps
spray-wall-apps.intro: A spray wall app starts with the wall you have. A home wall might just need a photo and a way to save problems. A gym might also want a setter to manage lists or run a comp. Here’s what Boardsesh, Stōkt and Retro Flash offer for those setups.
spray-wall-apps.compatibility: Boardsesh on iPhone and Android can detect holds from a photo and lets you edit the result. You can climb from the marked-up photo alone. Lighting requires mapped, compatible hardware, such as WLED over Wi-Fi.
spray-wall-apps.tradeoffs: Try Boardsesh if your spray wall sessions belong in the same logbook as your other boards, or if you want to share a live queue. Stōkt is worth a look if your gym wants paid setup help or tools for running competitions. Retro Flash is a fit if you set circuits, use your own grades or have a partly symmetrical wall.

photo.title: From wall photo to the first problem
photo.body: Take a straight-on photo so you have a clear view of the holds. In Boardsesh, you can add any the app misses or fix their outlines before setting. If you’d rather hand that work off, Stōkt offers a paid service that prepares the photo and maps the holds.

sharing.title: Who can get to your problems?
sharing.body: In Boardsesh, a home wall can stay private or be shared by link. You can also publish the wall or attach a private wall to a gym so its members can see it. A playlist can hold a circuit you want to repeat. Retro Flash supports circuits too, along with custom grades for walls that use their own scale.

reset.title: When the holds move
reset.body: Open the wall from the Climbs tab and choose Reset this Spraywall to replace the photo and review the new hold map. Publishing the reset archives the old wall with its problems. The sends in your logbook keep their original climbs.

setup.label: Set up a wall
setup.boardsesh: Start from a photo with hold detection and edit the marked holds. A wall can be Private, Link only or Public.
setup.stokt: Scan a wall from a phone and tidy the hold map in a desktop editor, or pay for managed setup.
setup.retroFlash: The developer lists support for adjustable and private walls, plus symmetrical and partly symmetrical hold layouts.

features.label: Set and share problems
features.boardsesh: Set on the wall photo, collect circuits in playlists and let a group add problems to a live queue.
features.stokt: Stōkt Pro lets a gym publish official climb lists, run competitions and set problems at different wall angles.
features.retroFlash: Set circuits or competition boulders and choose a built-in grading system or define one of your own.

lighting.label: Light the holds
lighting.boardsesh: WLED is optional and uses Wi-Fi once the holds are mapped. Bluetooth lighting requires hardware that Boardsesh supports.
lighting.stokt: Stōkt Pro lists LED support, with lighting kits and an option to connect your own LEDs.
lighting.retroFlash: LED compatibility is unspecified in the developer’s App Store and Google Play listings.

price.label: Price (checked Nov 24, 2026)
price.boardsesh: Boardsesh is free to download. If you want to light your wall, the compatible hardware is separate.
price.stokt: Start on a free home plan or choose a paid home or gym plan. Stōkt lists Pro at $20 per month.
price.retroFlash: Free download with in-app purchases. The US App Store lists the Home Wall Year Pass at $4.99.
